slides.heading: Phone Number Mnemonics
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Recursion
slides.narration: Let's solve Phone Number Mnemonics, a medium recursion problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: All letter strings a digit string could spell on a keypad (0 and 1 map to themselves).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. All letter strings a digit string could spell on a keypad (0 and 1 map to themselves).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Each digit maps to a few letters; explore every combination with backtracking.
slides.narration: Each digit maps to a few letters; explore every combination with backtracking.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Iterative: expand a list digit by digit (BFS)
slides.narration: You can expand a list of partial strings digit by digit, or backtrack depth first with one string builder. Both are bounded by four to the n times n, the size of the output.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Try each letter for the digit
3. At the end, record the word
slides.narration: Step by step. First, recurse digit by digit. Second, try each letter for the digit. Third, at the end, record the word.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: 1905 → letters per digit
slides.narration: For one-nine-zero-five, one and zero map to themselves, nine to w, x, y, z, and five to j, k, l.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Depth-first: one letter per digit
slides.narration: Recursion picks one letter per digit, depth first, then backtracks to try the next letter.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: 12 mnemonics = 1 × 4 × 1 × 3
slides.narration: In total there are 12 mnemonics: one times four times one times three.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Build recurses on the digit index. At the end it records the string; otherwise for each letter of the current key it appends, recurses and removes the letter.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of 4 to the n times n. Space is O of 4 to the n times n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: In this version zero and one map to themselves. Remove the last character after each recursive call.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: only dictionary words (use a trie)
slides.narration: State the output-size bound clearly. Restricting to real words is a nice trie follow-up.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Each digit maps to a few letters; explore every combination with backtracking.
slides.narration: To recap Phone Number Mnemonics: Each digit maps to a few letters; explore every combination with backtracking. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
